newsitem.title: UK: Dlr recovers ground vs mark and yen in late Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dlr recovers ground vs mark and yen in late Europe.

text.p: The dollar recovered composure against the mark and yen in late Europe to stand near session peaks against both units after a boost from bargain-hunting.
"(The dollar) went a bit too far. Most people are still bullish on the dollar and looking to buy it on the dips," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank.
Earlier the dollar drifted to over two-week lows of 1.6853 marks as the German unit probed new highs on background European Monetary Union (EMU) jitters.
At 1545 dollar/mark stood at 1.6895/00 marks, off session lows, but still down from 1.6954/64 marks in late Europe on Friday.
Against the yen, however, the dollar ended a touch firmer at 123.63/3.73 yen vs 123.30/40 in late Europe on Friday.
Analysts said a 6.5 percent rise in Japan's February trade surplus, the first in over two years, was widely expected and therefore had little effect on dollar/yen.

The dollar scaled higher on Monday against sterling after long-awaited news on a date for the British election sparked profit-taking on long sterling positions. Analysts said they were surprised by the drop, given that May 1 had been a favoured date. At 1603 sterling stood at $1.5865/75 vs $1.6025/35 in late Europe on Friday.
"In London, I think it is fair to say that sterling has been the main focus," said a currency trader.

Some currency analysts, however, said dollar markets could be a touch jittery ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting on March 25 as opinion remains divided over what action, if any, the Fed will take over monetary policy.
Dealers, for instance, have said soft U.S. producer price data released on Friday has helped cool speculation of higher rates.
February's producer price index dropped by 0.4 percent, its largest fall since October 1994, figures showed on Friday.
"There is nervousness ahead of the Fed. Will they or won't they (raise rates)?," said Commerzbank's Ferridge.
